summary: A humorous feature on how community theaters create inventive sets with tiny budgets. It covers plywood, recycling, thrift-store finds, illusion, salvaged projectors, and a 'Good Enough' philosophy, illustrated by anecdotes about named local theater figures in late 2023. It concludes that imagination makes up for the lack of funding.
one_line: A comic tribute to community theater set designers who turn plywood, recycled junk, thrift finds and old projectors into convincing sets on shoestring budgets.
key_facts: Marjorie Splint, a set guru known since the 'Great Plywood Drought of November 2023', advises treating plywood 'like it's straight out of Versailles'.
On October 2, 2023, Gertrude Stuffings, prop master at Little-Town-That-Could-Playhouse, crafted a chandelier out of plastic bottles.
Gertrude Stuffings declared, 'Who needs Broadway budgets when you've got a recycling bin full of dreams?'
Recycling led community theaters across the state to reuse items: egg cartons became cobblestones, old tires became town fountains, and bubble wrap became nearly everything.
On September 15, 2023, director Frederick von Throwpenny shopped at the 'Vintage Finds and Thoughts' thrift store and found a worn velvet loveseat.
Frederick von Throwpenny christened the loveseat the 'Throne of the Realm'; the audience suspected real royal funding despite a laughable budget.
In early December 2023, Bethany Mirage turned cardboard and strategic lighting into a convincing fortress for the play 'The Siege of Cardboard Castle'.
Old-school projectors salvaged from the local high school's throw-away pile are used for holographic-like effects.
On September 23, 2023, director Charlie Beamspot found a way to tie twelve projectors together with string, spit, and a prayer.
On September 30, 2023, Billie Halfmeasure, a motivational speaker and set designer, gave the speech 'When the Budget's Tight, The Tight Get 'Good Enough''.
Under Halfmeasure's 'Good Enough' philosophy, a golden goblet can be a spray-painted yogurt cup and an ancient manuscript a scribbled-on menu from Tony's Pizza Palace.
Designer Jimmy Bracket's garage DIY table is cited as the kind of origin a plywood prop might have before appearing on stage.
